newsitem.title: UK: UK minister confirms plan for late payment bill.
newsitem.headline: UK minister confirms plan for late payment bill.

text.p: Junior trade and industry minister Babara Roche on Tuesday confirmed a press report that the government plans to introduce a bill soon to give firms the right to claim interest on the late payment of invoices.
Roche, whose brief includes the small business sector, told BBC radio: "What we are proposing is to give a right to small firms to go to court to claim interest on late payment."

Roche said the government planned to consult widely on the way in which this should be done, but confirmed that the bill would be included in Wednesday's Queen's Speech setting out the government's legislative programme for the next 1-1/2 years.
She said the government did not envisage the bill provoking a rush of court cases.
But she added: "It will be a very valuable weapon for the small businesses to use and by using this and other methods we will get that very important change in commercial culture."

The Times newspaper said the bill would offer a two billion stg lifeline to Britain's small firms, but Ian Peters, deputy director general at the British Chambers of Commerce, was less enthusiastic about the move.
"I think the legislation is ill-conceived. The worry has to be that it will backfire," Peters said.

He said in the long run small businesses could suffer because customers, unwilling to risk being charged interest, would insist on contract terms which gave them longer to pay. -- London Newsroom +44 171 5427767
